reasoning_content:
Root is consistently 200 on fresh server. Now let me check whether the missing files are tracked in git or were expected to be generated by postinstall. They are gitignored (assets/data/.gitignore ignores *). So they must be generated by postinstall. The postinstall failed for these 3 files due to missing credentials.

Let me check the git status to see what the repo considers modified/untracked. Also confirm the scripts are the ones needing credentials. Already read them.

Let me also verify whether a production build would work (the guide's primary requirement is yarn dev though). The guide only says yarn install + yarn dev, access at localhost:3000. Given root returns 200, one could argue partial success. But 5+ routes (the main dashboard pages) all return 500. The "separate pages for each of the four categories" are the core of the app description, and all are broken.

Actually, let me reconsider: the task says success = "complete and the software is operational according to the supplied guide." The guide says "You should now be able to access the application at http://localhost:3000." That works (200). But the app is a dashboard with category pages; those are the primary functionality.

However, I should consider the possibility that these missing data files are expected to be absent in this environment regardless, and the failure is due to missing external credentials, not installation. But the installation guide's yarn install should produce a working app. The summary explicitly acknowledges the incomplete state. Since these credentials aren't part of the guide, following the guide alone yields a broken app.

Hmm, but there's nuance: Is it possible the app was in a healthy state before and my testing caused the 500s? No — missing files are missing on disk.

Let me double-check whether maybe a build (yarn build) was intended and the guide's yarn dev is what matters. Either way missing source files break compilation.

Let me verify git status to see if missing files were ever present.

Also verify root page actually isn't importing the broken component — root works, so it isn't.

Let me also check that the assets/data missing files maybe exist somewhere else (e.g., in git history). Let me check git ls-files.

I think I have enough. Let me do a couple more confirmations: check package install integrity via a quick check that next binary exists and node_modules has key deps. And verify no build errors from missing modules beyond these.

Let me finalize. Actually let me test one more thing: whether the app can start at all with `yarn start` after a build — not needed since guide is dev.

Let me verify git status of assets/data and git log for these files.
